note.backdrop: The morning's rebound became one of the largest up days in years, on a single piece of company news: at 8:55 a.m. ET Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, 11 days after he resigned. By the check the S&P 500 was +4.8%, the Nasdaq 100 +7.1%, small caps +3.3% and the VIX -22.9%; semiconductors' median +12.6%, against +5.8% before the open. Nasdaq futures hit CME's 7% overnight limit for the first time since it was set in 2020. Gold +4.2% and bitcoin +4.3% rose with stocks again. Only 4 of 2451 stocks are outside their 9-in-10 range: Nvidia, Kymera and Capricor on their own news, GigaCloud with no event found.

read.says: At 11:03 a.m. ET: QQQ +6.98%, SPY +4.82%, Nvidia +33.55% (board reinstated Huang at 8:55 a.m. ET, up from +8.04% at 8:02); Zscaler 3.7% below the value of 1.135 CrowdStrike shares ($220.91 against $229.41); Zscaler owes a $1.4 billion fee in some cases; Capricor says cash and investments of about $198.5 million at Sept 30 fund at least 12 months; HPE and Symbotic report after today's close.

singles.beneath: +36.1% since Friday's close, +32.1% after the market and drivers; about $157 against Friday's $115.31. The desk's call 63a7bc55 (15% either way from $124.06 by Nov 27) stands about 26% above $124.06; it is judged at the Nov 27 close. A Phase 3 is planned by mid-2027.
singles.cause: BROADEN2: its oral eczema pill KT-621 met its primary and secondary goals at every dose; Jefferies said the 40-point gap over placebo cleared its benchmark and skin and itch results were broadly in line with dupilumab's, with conjunctivitis manageable and no patient stopping KT-621 for it (s5).

singles.beneath: -76.6%. A correction to this morning's note: the case file's 1.2 quarters counts cash only; Capricor says cash and investments of about $198.5 million at Sept 30 fund its plans for at least 12 months (StockTitan, citing its release). The inspection findings go to the trial's integrity, not only its size, which is why a third filing on the same data looks harder (inferred).
singles.cause: The FDA's second Complete Response Letter for deramiocel. Beyond the evidence falling short, an FDA inspection found unauthorized changes to the statistical analysis plan after the fact and breaches of the procedures that keep treatment assignments hidden, and the FDA sent a separate Regulatory Responsibility Letter (s2).

singles.beneath: -13.2%, deeper than -9.2% before the open; on this market it is -18.9% of its own.
singles.cause: Monro suspended its quarterly cash dividend.

themes.beneath: The stock had fallen about a third since the CEO resigned on Nov 12 (memory of the Nov 12-20 notes); Friday alone it fell 14.01%. Before the open, with only the dip-buying story, Nvidia was about +8%; it went to +26.8% by 9:01 a.m. ET after the release and +33.6% at 11:03 (StockTitan). So most of today's chip move rests on one board decision, not on new numbers about demand. Not every AI name joined: Anthropic, listed Thursday, was down (s12), and a report says lenders against GPUs now want 50-60% loan-to-value, down from 80% (s31, opinion-level, not checked).
themes.cause: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director, effective immediately, saying input from senior levels of the US government left it confident his return poses no national security risk; a committee of independent directors continues its investigation, and Nvidia keeps cooperating with government inquiries (its 8-K release).
themes.mechanism: Nvidia moved most on its own (+24.0% after the market and its industry). Its suppliers, customers and the AI hosts rose with it, but for most of them the move is their beta to a +5-7% market: Lattice +14.8% with the market carrying +15.3% at beta 3.18; Marvell +18.2% with +16.6%; Texas Instruments +9.7% with +8.4%; NXP +8.3% with +8.4%; Tesla +12.2% with +9.4%. CoreWeave keeps +7.6% of its own, Dell +8.9%.
